archetypes.name: call-site-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: The plan claims a specific 90-line contiguous block at SKILL.md lines 1193–1282 as the sole replacement surface; verify those bounds, contiguity, and that no scattered duplicates exist.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the inline disposition-gate block the plan claims to replace (skills/implement/SKILL.md lines 1193–1282) is (a) actually contiguous, (b) the only occurrence of the merge-base / find / awk input-resolution logic in SKILL.md, and (c) that the thin-call replacement snippet the plan specifies (the six-line set+e / direct-path invocation) is inserted at exactly that site with no leftover inline fragments. Check whether the surrounding prose references — NEVER #17, NEVER #18, the helper-inventory paragraph — are updated consistently or whether the plan leaves stale cross-references. Flag any line-range drift or split-block shapes that would cause the replacement to be incomplete. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: script-contract-drift
archetypes.rationale: The plan hard-wires specific flag names for append-tool-failure.sh, oos-disposition-gate.sh, and oos-non-security-block-count.awk; any drift between plan and actual CLIs silently mis-wires the helper.
archetypes.prompt_body: Cross-check every flag the plan specifies against the real scripts: (1) append-tool-failure.sh — confirm --site, --tool, --exit-code, --category, --output-file, --redact exist and accept the values the plan passes; (2) oos-disposition-gate.sh — confirm --fork-mode, --repo-unavailable, --oos-issues-ndjson, --accepted-files, --filed-urls-file, --filed-urls-strict-file, --commit-range are the actual accepted flags and that exit codes 0/1/2 map to the semantics the plan assigns; (3) oos-non-security-block-count.awk — confirm the file exists at the path the plan resolves ($SCRIPT_DIR/oos-non-security-block-count.awk) and accepts the per-file invocation pattern described. Also verify the script-md-siblings rule (.claude/rules/script-md-siblings.md) and confirm the plan's .md content spec satisfies it. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-structural-gap
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds a substantial set of new test cases to test-oos-disposition-gate.sh and assumes specific infrastructure (mkitmp, assert_rc, GIT_TMP, ORPHAN_TMP, execution-issues.md) that may not yet exist in the harness.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit skills/implement/scripts/test-oos-disposition-gate.sh for the helpers the plan assumes are available or proposes to add: mkitmp (fake implement-tmpdir seeding), assert_rc, GIT_TMP / ORPHAN_TMP fixture environments, and execution-issues.md as the append-tool-failure.sh output target. Verify the Makefile target test-oos-disposition-gate is registered and exercisable standalone. Check whether the plan's FINDING_4 assertion ('assert execution-issues.md contains Tool Failures with step-8-oos-checkpoint') is achievable given how append-tool-failure.sh actually writes that file — confirm the grep patterns the plan implies will match real output. Flag any test cases in the plan that depend on infrastructure the harness does not currently provide and the plan does not explicitly add. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
